WHAT SHIPPED: (1) tools/runner stamps the enumerated killed_by (none|provider-limit|provider-auth|provider-connection|directive|wall|cpu|rss|liveness|watchdog|harness-error) into its OWN run record on every kill path (launch directive refusal, mid-run directive poll, the guard loop, runner exception) — the runner is the only process that knows which guard fired; T634's coordinate (the runner emits the reason for liveness kills into the vocabulary this row defines). (2) tools/dispatch_verify.py derives killed_by from the runner's terminal record (the runner's own stamp first, then killed/kill_class/signal/exit, then the D021 window-constrained refusal classifier ONLY for the cases the record cannot answer: a harness kill whose tail window shows the refusal that CAUSED it (T616 shape), a non-zero exit with no harness kill (T617 shape), no record at all) and appends killed_by=<enum> to EVERY ledger line (appended at the END so every pre-existing substring assertion on verified=/fail=/reason= still matches). The broad-grep false positives (T526/T601) are structurally impossible: the classifier scans only the first+last 8 KiB of worker output, and both quotes sat mid-log.
